column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/pleme-helm.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. On 2026-08-08 pleme-io/graphql-synthesizer ran
# cargo-auto-release. The run reported SUCCESS: `bump` bumped, tagged and
# pushed; `ship` was SKIPPED; the crate was never published; nothing said so.
# The condition that skipped it was correct and deliberate. The failure was
# that nobody had written down WHICH JOBS MUST RUN for a given input, so a
# deliberate skip and a broken skip produced the same green tick.
# WHAT THIS WORKFLOW IS. pleme-helm is a TIER-2 COMPOSER for the `helm` family:
# three jobs, zero `needs`, zero steps of its own, each job a bare `uses:`
# gated only by `inputs.target == '<that job's own name>'`. The entire file is
# one switch on one string. So the only axis is `inputs.target`, and the table
# is one row per arm plus the two rows no arm covers.
# THE FAILURE THIS TABLE IS AGAINST is a SHARPER version of the
# graphql-synthesizer one, not a milder one. A pure dispatcher has no
# catch-all and no default: hand it a target that matches no `if:` and all
# three jobs skip, the workflow finishes having done nothing at all, and
# GitHub reports SUCCESS. There is not even a `bump` that ran to make the run
# look half-alive — the run is entirely empty and entirely green. Rows 4 and 5
# write that state down, so "dispatched nothing" stops being indistinguishable
# from "dispatched something".
# WHY ALL THREE JOBS PUBLISH AND THIS TABLE STILL CARRIES NO PRIVACY KEY.
# Every leaf here ships artifacts — helm-auto-release and
# helm-monorepo-auto-release package and push charts to the OCI registry,
# helm-publish publishes. None of that is gated HERE: pleme-helm reads no
# `github.event.repository.private`, no toggle input, nothing but `target`.
# The do-it / don't-do-it pair for THIS file is therefore
# target-selects-a-leaf (rows 1-3) versus target-selects-nothing (rows 4-5).
# Adding a visibility key would mean inventing a context value that no
# condition in this workflow reads. The privacy question is real but belongs
# to each leaf's own table — helm-auto-release.cases.tsv answers it there, and
# records that `ship` publishes from a private caller too.
# ROW 4 IS THE ROW THAT WOULD ROT IF LEFT OUT. `helm-chart-release` is a REAL
# substrate reusable and an entirely plausible thing to pass alongside
# `family: helm` — but it is deliberately NOT a member of this composer. It
# nests a reusable of its own, so routing it through a tier-2 composer would
# make the call chain 5 deep and GitHub would refuse to start the run; pleme.yml
# dispatches it directly instead (`direct-helm-chart-release`). Row 4 pins that
# a caller who guesses wrong gets a silent empty green, and the day someone
# adds a fourth job for it here, row 4 flips to RAN and the change lands as a
# decision. `helm-unittest` is a second non-member of the same kind.
# TABLE RULES, restated because they are what make these rows look redundant
# on purpose:
#   - every context path any condition reads must be declared in EVERY case;
#     an undeclared path is an ERROR, never an empty default, so an incomplete
#     case can never turn into a confident verdict;
#   - an EMPTY value (`inputs.target=`) is a distinct state from any named
#     value. Here it models the caller's own detect/route step producing
#     nothing, which is precisely the input a switch with no catch-all handles
#     worst — and `target` being `required: true` does not save it, because
#     GitHub accepts an empty string for a required string input.
# NOT ASSERTED, because it is outside what job selection can see: that the
# selected leaf file exists, that the leaf's own jobs then select correctly
# (its own table's problem), or that the 4-level nesting cap still holds. This
# table proves WHICH of the three jobs is selected, and nothing past that.
# 1. The helm-auto-release arm. Its two siblings must skip — a composer that
#    fans out to more than one leaf per target would double-publish.
target-helm-auto-release
# 2. The helm-monorepo-auto-release arm.
target-helm-monorepo-auto-release
# 3. The helm-publish arm.
target-helm-publish
# 4. The catch-all that does not exist. `helm-chart-release` is a real
#    reusable, deliberately dispatched from pleme.yml directly rather than
#    from here (it nests, so chain depth would hit 5). Passing it as this
#    composer's target selects NOTHING and the run is green. Intended
#    behaviour today; asserted so a future fourth job is a visible decision.
target-unrouted-sibling
# 5. Empty target — "the caller routed, but produced no target". Distinct from
#    any named value and from row 4: nothing was mistyped, nothing was chosen.
#    All three skip, the run is green, and this row is the only place that
#    says so.
target-empty
